original_question: Let 1 < a1 < a2 < ... be an infinite sequence of integers with no three-term arithmetic progression. Must the reciprocal sum sum_{n>1} 1/a_n always be less than 2, and is the map sending such a sequence to its reciprocal sum bijective? More generally, if a sequence is constructed to avoid tuples satisfying a given functional relation f(a_{i1},...,a_{im}) = a_{i,m+1}, determine the maximum possible reciprocal sum.
target_in_paper: Unsolved Problem 28 ("On a problem with infinite sequences"), specifically the question about reciprocal sums for infinite increasing integer sequences with no 3-term arithmetic progression, together with its immediate generalization to sequences avoiding tuples satisfying f(a_{i_1},...,a_{i_m}) = a_{i_{m+1}}. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core content of Unsolved Problem 28 almost verbatim: the hypothesis 1 < a_1 < a_2 < ...; avoidance of 3-term arithmetic progressions; the question whether sum_{n>1} 1/a_n is always < 2; the question about the reciprocal-sum map being bijective; and the paper’s own broader reformulation using a function f and forbidden tuples of sequence elements. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
missing_details: In the paper, the first part is about increasing sequences of integers, but the generalization is not: it asks for 0 < a_1 < a_2 < ... and a function f:(0,∞)^m -> (0,∞), so the ambient set in the general case is the positive reals, not just the integers. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The meaning of "bijective" is not fully stand-alone unless the codomain of S is specified. The paper writes "Is the function S({a_n}) = sum_{n>1} 1/a_n bijective?" without explicitly naming the codomain, so a refined question should say whether this means onto (0,2) or onto the image of S. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

For the generalized forbidden-pattern condition, the paper does not explicitly state whether the indices i_1,...,i_{m+1} must be distinct; a stand-alone formulation should say "no tuple of terms from the sequence" or explicitly impose distinctness. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The paper’s indexing is slightly ambiguous in the available text: it states 1 < a_1 and writes sum_{n>1} 1/a_n, but the geometric example on the same page appears to suggest a series beginning with 1. A cleaned-up stand-alone version should fix the indexing convention explicitly. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

To match the paper exactly, the generalization should be phrased as: for fixed m and fixed f, maximize sum_{n>1} 1/a_n over all admissible strictly increasing sequences satisfying the stated avoidance property. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let A be the family of all infinite strictly increasing sequences of integers 1 < a_1 < a_2 < ... such that no three terms of the sequence form an arithmetic progression, and define S((a_n)) = sum_{n>1} 1/a_n. Is it true that S((a_n)) < 2 for every (a_n) in A, and, if so, does every real value in (0,2) arise from exactly one such sequence? More generally, for a fixed integer m >= 1 and a fixed function f:(0,∞)^m -> (0,∞), among all strictly increasing positive sequences 0 < a_1 < a_2 < ... for which there is no tuple of terms (a_{i_1},...,a_{i_m},a_{i_{m+1}}) satisfying f(a_{i_1},...,a_{i_m}) = a_{i_{m+1}}, determine the maximum possible value of sum_{n>1} 1/a_n. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because Unsolved Problem 28 is the only place in the paper that combines all three features present in your draft: the infinite progression-free sequence, the reciprocal-sum bound < 2, and the question about bijectivity of the reciprocal-sum map; it then immediately states the broader f-based avoidance problem with the same reciprocal-sum objective. Nearby Problem 24 concerns finite subsets avoiding m-ary relations, but it asks for the maximum number of extracted elements rather than a reciprocal-sum extremum, so it is a neighboring problem rather than the exact target. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
